sources.population: Taiwan Biobank: 14,537 adults (6,184 men; 8,353 women), ages 30-70, recruited in 2012-2016; volunteer/genotyping-selected cohort.
sources.measurement: HDL-C in mg/dL; biochemical examination. Maintext does not provide a complete HDL assay method or assay harmonization with target.
sources.cohort_overlap: Likely substantial but unquantified participant overlap with H2019; not independent corroboration. No identified overlap with target; both source populations are distinct cohorts.

sources.population: Taiwan Biobank: 9,075 adults (4,262 men; 4,813 women), ages 30-70.
sources.measurement: HDL-C in mg/dL, measured during biochemical examination; detailed assay unknown in inspected maintext.
sources.cohort_overlap: Likely overlapping Taiwan Biobank participants with G2019; overlap count unknown; not a replication.

sources.population: 28,090 patients: 14,121 women and 13,969 men; geography, age range, selection, follow-up duration and full adjustment not established by the approved abstract.
sources.measurement: Changes in HDL-C; HDL subfraction apo A1 concentrations measured using two-dimensional HDL-mapping. Exact total HDL-C assay unknown.
sources.cohort_overlap: No reported link to Taiwan Biobank in abstract; independence cannot be established fully from abstract; no individual data accessed.

sources.population: GRAPHIC UK white European nuclear families; 1,932 analyzed individuals, ages 18-61, 49% male.
sources.measurement: HDL-C and cholesterol efflux capacity (CEC) are separate measures; serum lipids by ultracentrifugation or NMR; detailed methods in external supplement unavailable here.
sources.cohort_overlap: Separate UK cohort, distinct from Taiwan Biobank; no known target overlap.

sources.population: 1,214 consecutive overweight/obesity clinic patients in Bari/Apulia, Italy, 2018-2019, all described as Caucasian. No medications (including oral contraceptives); excluded diabetes, endocrine disease, chronic inflammatory disease, stable hypertension, clinical cardiovascular disease, malignancy, renal/liver failure and inherited thrombocytopenia. Table 1 age 39.50 +/-12.61, range14-74; BMI33.89 +/-6.08, range25-64.60. Text reports slightly different age/BMI ranges and sex counts; these discrepancies are retained, not reconciled. BMI>30 subgroup n not given in the embedded response table.
sources.measurement: Overnight-fasting blood, plasma lipids including HDL-C by automated colorimetric method (Hitachi; Boehringer Mannheim). This is not an established calibration to the target direct-serum Roche assay.
sources.cohort_overlap: Independent Italian clinical cohort; no identified overlap with Taiwan Biobank, GRAPHIC or target. No participant records accessed.

evidence.locator: Table 2, Sex rows; BMI category column headings; Methods 2.2
evidence.estimand: Unadjusted arithmetic mean HDL-C within each sex-by-BMI category
evidence.adjustment: None; stratified by sex and BMI category; age and other covariates remain mixed within cells.
evidence.uncertainty: Rounded group means; SEMs and n are in G02. Not conditional means at an exact BMI or age.
evidence.applicability: Reasonably broad adult cohort but Asian volunteer sample, different BMI distribution and incomplete assay comparability; ages outside 30-70 require extrapolation.
evidence.model_use: Anchor sex-specific conditional means after age centering; do not use a fully adjusted BMI coefficient as a marginal coefficient.

evidence.locator: Table 2, Sex rows; Methods 2.4 explicitly defines continuous results as mean +/- standard error
evidence.estimand: Standard errors of cell arithmetic means and cell sample counts, not individual standard deviations
evidence.uncertainty: SEs are rounded to two decimals. SE*sqrt(n) presumes conventional unweighted mean SE and independent observations; the paper does not give a residual SD for a model using only BMI, sex and age.
evidence.applicability: Supports heteroskedastic individual variability within broad sex-BMI categories; conditional-on-exact-predictor and target variances are uncertain.
evidence.model_use: Convert each SEM to aggregate individual SD using SE*sqrt(n); use the resulting CV as conditional variability proxy.

evidence.locator: Table 3, Age rows; model covariates listed in table
evidence.estimand: Adjusted additive HDL-C contrasts by age category relative to ages 30-40
evidence.adjustment: Table includes exercise, WHR category, BMI category, body fat category, sex, smoking, alcohol, coffee and vegetarian diet. It is not a model adjusted only for the observed target fields.
evidence.uncertainty: SE/CI not reported in table; overlapping 40-year boundary in printed category labels is preserved as a source ambiguity. Common-sex contrasts do not establish a sex-by-age interaction.
evidence.applicability: Age association may change when omitted covariates are marginalized; cross-sectional contrasts are not aging effects.
evidence.model_use: Smooth interpolation of the reported contrasts with no numerical sex-age interaction; category centers and extrapolation are declared assumptions.

evidence.locator: Table 2, Age rows, counts within each BMI column
evidence.estimand: Empirical counts of age groups conditional on BMI category, pooled across sex
evidence.uncertainty: Counts are exact as printed but joint sex-by-age-by-BMI counts unavailable.
evidence.applicability: Source centering only; not imposed on target predictor distributions.
evidence.model_use: Within each source BMI category subtract the count-weighted mean age contrast from each sex-specific HDL anchor.

evidence.locator: Table 3 BMI and age rows; Table 1 and Results paragraph 1
evidence.estimand: Adjusted sex-specific BMI category contrasts and reported descriptive means
evidence.adjustment: Includes genotype, age, diet, exercise, smoking, second-hand smoke, alcohol, tea, WHR, LDL-C, triglycerides, diabetes and hypertension.
evidence.uncertainty: Table 1 prints male/female SEMs 0.171/0.191 whereas prose prints 0.191/0.171. Underweight/normal count rows appear swapped, but no correction is asserted. Some regression row labels also have unexplained extra numbers.
evidence.applicability: Same parent cohort as G2019; heavier adjustment (including TG and WHR) changes the estimand.
evidence.model_use: Qualitative compatibility and extraction warning only; no parameters or residual scales obtained from the inconsistent fields.

evidence.locator: Approved Europe PMC abstract, Results and Conclusions
evidence.estimand: Longitudinal percent change in HDL-C per change in BMI, expressed relative to baseline HDL-C
evidence.adjustment: Abstract says age- and sex-adjusted subfraction measurements; exact adjustment for each total HDL-C relation is not established.

reported.direction_across_obesity_classes: HDL-C decreased with weight-category gain and increased with weight-category loss across multiple classes

evidence.uncertainty: Abstract only, no total HDL-C slope SE/CI, no baseline mean by sex, no fulltext or numerical tail cross-sectional estimate available.
evidence.applicability: Within-person weight-change associations are not between-person BMI effects; clinical selection and population comparability uncertain.
evidence.model_use: Retained for provenance of the initial version and its sensitivity comparator only. No final numerical parameter uses this longitudinal slope.

evidence.locator: Results: relationships, stability and heritability; Materials and Methods
evidence.estimand: Distinction between HDL-C concentration and cholesterol efflux capacity plus evidence of stable non-predictor variation
evidence.adjustment: Varies by analysis; not extracted as an HDL-on-BMI model.
evidence.uncertainty: Not a conditional residual variance estimate. Tabular HDL summaries are rendered as images and unavailable in approved text; linked external supplement not retrieved.
evidence.applicability: Independent cohort supports avoiding the substitution of HDL-function effects for HDL-C effects; does not establish target calibration.
evidence.model_use: Context only. Do not import CEC regression coefficients, repeatability or heritability as residual SD.

evidence.locator: Main article Table 2, HDL row, BMI column; table footnote and Statistics
evidence.estimand: Linear cross-sectional additive HDL-C slope per kg/m^2 BMI among participants with BMI>=25
evidence.adjustment: Age and sex. Each anthropometric parameter modeled separately; no simultaneous WHR/TG adjustment for this HDL regression.
evidence.uncertainty: A common-sex linear coefficient over BMI25-64.6, not a spline or exact tail curve. Age/sex coefficients and conditional residual SD unavailable. Selected clinical population; some adolescents included.
evidence.applicability: Outcome and cross-sectional regression estimand align better than a within-person change coefficient; the clinical exclusions, geography, age range and assay still limit transport.
evidence.model_use: Cross-sectional contextual comparison; BMI>30 subgroup estimate L02 is selected for the continuation, so this coefficient is not pooled or counted as independent evidence.

evidence.locator: Published Author response to Decision Letter 0, 30 Aug 2020, response to Reviewer 2 minor point2; Table rev2, HDL row, BMI column; embedded directly in approved JATS/text (DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0241841.r002)
evidence.estimand: Linear cross-sectional additive HDL-C slope per kg/m^2 BMI restricted to BMI>30
evidence.adjustment: Table rev2 footnote: adjusted for age and gender; anthropometric predictors analyzed separately.
evidence.uncertainty: This subgroup result appears in the published response table rather than the main final article table. Subgroup n, sex-specific slopes, residual SD, age coefficients and nonlinear shape are unavailable. Same cohort as L01, not independent replication. CI is source sampling uncertainty, not target transport uncertainty.
evidence.applicability: Directly addresses between-person obesity slope with adjustment for the available predictors; still a drug-naive, disease-excluded Italian clinic sample including adolescents. No direct information beyond source BMI maximum about64.6.
evidence.model_use: Replace longitudinal tail with common additive slope -0.33 at final anchor; use a positivity-preserving exponential continuation and check flat/source-CI/linear/initial alternatives.

evidence.locator: Main Table 1 HDL row and Clinical, anthropometric and biochemical parameters assessment
evidence.estimand: Overall unadjusted HDL-C mean/SD/range and measurement method in a selected mixed-sex obesity cohort

reported.assay: automated colorimetric plasma lipid assay, Hitachi/Boehringer Mannheim

evidence.uncertainty: Overall SD mixes sex, BMI, age and unmeasured factors; it is not a conditional residual scale. Table/prose disagree slightly on other cohort summaries, though this HDL row is unambiguous.
evidence.applicability: Provides assay context and a dispersion comparison but no assay-equivalence factor, no exact-predictor residual variance and no target-matched distribution.
evidence.model_use: Context only; do not replace source-cell SD with overall mixed-sex SD or treat source minimum/maximum as truncation limits.
